title: DramaRama
role: Founder & AI Engineer, Whimsy & Rigor LLC
summary: Multi-agent LLM coaching platform: an intake agent interviews you and routes you to one of twelve advisor agents, which coach you through a stuck problem on a canvas without handing you the answer.
description:
You bring a real problem in plain words. An intake agent interviews you, reads how you're stuck, and routes you to the one of twelve advisor agents whose way of thinking fits. The advisor runs a short exercise with you on a node-based canvas, reacting to what you write but never supplying the answer. Built on Edward Burger's 5 Elements of Effective Thinking.

The orchestration is declarative: a spec file defines the models, context sources and node graph, and a runtime executes it. Every node execution and model call becomes a structured trace event (assembled context with token estimates, input, output, decision reasons, usage, latency) that streams live over SSE and is written as JSONL per run, so any session can be replayed. Backstage, a workbench I built on top of that, renders the orchestration as a graph, lists runs, and lets you step through every trace event and edit prompts in place.

Guardrails run in two layers: advisor prompts never supply a question, an answer or a reframe, and a separate LLM judge reviews each turn for engagement with the exercise, never for correctness. Per-user token budgets meter every model call; Clerk JWTs are validated against a cached JWKS with key rotation handled, with a per-endpoint ownership audit. FastAPI backend in a hexagonal layout, 199 pytest tests, 41 versioned Postgres migrations whose names record six product pivots. Next.js and TypeScript front end on Vercel; API on AWS EC2 behind a server-side proxy.

About fifty in-person user interviews in Austin, plus feedback from the framework's author, a C-suite PR advisor and a founder coach, drove those pivots.
highlights: Declarative orchestration spec and runtime with per-node tracing, replayable runs and a Backstage workbench to inspect them
Two-layer guardrails (prompt rules plus an LLM engagement judge), per-user token budgets with metering, Clerk JWKS auth with an ownership audit
199 tests, 41 migrations recording six pivots driven by about fifty user interviews; built and run by one person

title: Sky City Trucking
role: Freelance developer: built, deployed, still supports
client: Trucking and logistics company, Fife, WA
summary: Marketing and driver-recruiting site for a trucking and logistics company near the Port of Tacoma, in English, Russian and Ukrainian. Built 2022–2023 from a UX designer's layouts, deployed on AWS, with fixes and paid updates since.
description:
Sky City is a family-owned trucking and logistics company in Fife, WA: port drayage, intermodal, over-the-road and a warehouse with transloading. The site had to work for two audiences, shippers requesting quotes and drivers applying for work, so it carries both a contact form and a driver application form, each validated with Joi, protected with reCAPTCHA and delivered through EmailJS, and it's fully translated into English, Russian and Ukrainian with i18next, which matters for the drivers it recruits.

I owned the project end to end with the company's VP: took the handoff from the UX designer's desktop, tablet and phone layouts, built the site in React with React Bootstrap and Sass, deployed it on AWS Amplify and set up the domain on Route 53. When the site went down in 2025 I recovered it, turned on auto-renewal and wrote step-by-step AWS instructions so the company could manage its own account. In 2026, four years in, the company's president brought me back for a paid rewrite of the Home, About and Capabilities pages.
highlights: End to end: design handoff, React build, AWS Amplify and Route 53, outage recovery with self-service docs for the client
Full translations in English, Russian and Ukrainian with i18next; contact and driver-application forms with Joi, reCAPTCHA and EmailJS
Four years of repeat paid work from the same client, most recently a content rewrite in 2026

title: V&Y Horizon
summary: Next.js marketing site for a Portland trucking carrier whose owner edits the content in Hygraph; redeployed in days when the client's domain lapsed in 2024.
description:
V&Y Horizon is a trucking carrier in Portland, OR: LTL cartage, rail and port drayage, intermodal. The owner wanted the business represented accurately and wanted to change copy without calling a developer, so the content model (headline copy, services, partner logos, customer reviews) lives in Hygraph and is fetched over GraphQL into a Next.js App Router site styled with React Bootstrap and Sass.

I ran the project between the owner and the UX designer: gathered the copy and assets, shared design previews, ran three rounds of corrections, and built the Next.js site in September–October 2023. The contact form validates with Joi, sits behind reCAPTCHA and delivers through EmailJS; the quote modal and careers application form validate with Joi. When the client's domain lapsed in June 2024, I registered it on Route 53 and had the site redeployed within days.
highlights: Client-editable content model in Hygraph, fetched over GraphQL into Next.js
Ran requirements and three correction rounds directly with a non-technical owner
Domain lost in June 2024: registered on Route 53 and redeployed within days

title: Fantum
role: Lead developer (contract, under a statement of work)
summary: React Native (Expo) job-board app led for a founder under a formal statement of work: Firebase auth with email and phone verification, Redux Toolkit state and the core app screens. The client discontinued the project before launch.
description:
Led development of a React Native (Expo) job-board app for a founder under a formal statement of work: Firebase auth with email and phone verification (Twilio Verify), Redux Toolkit state, and the core app screens. Prototyped pulling listings from job boards in the 2021 build. The client discontinued the project before launch.

The work ran from a signed statement of work in December 2021, revised in 2022, with weekly client meetings into 2024. I worked with a UX designer and a second developer, building from the designer's 2022 screens: applicant and recruiter onboarding, a multi-step registration flow with Joi validation, resume upload and the main app screens, styled with NativeWind. It's shown here as a recording only.
highlights: Led the build for a non-technical founder under a statement of work with status reporting and change control
Firebase auth with email and phone verification through Twilio Verify; Redux Toolkit registration state
Worked with a UX designer and a second developer over roughly three years of weekly meetings

title: Optimal Exterior
summary: Cleared a Google 'Deceptive Site' blacklisting on the company's WordPress site in about 48 hours, then rebuilt it in React in 2022; the new quote form brought in about nine real quote requests in its first three months.
description:
Optimal Exterior is a residential exterior-cleaning company in the Houston area. The first site, in 2021, was WordPress with SEO and Search Console set up. In November 2021 Google flagged it as a 'Deceptive Site' and blacklisted it; I ran the malware scan, removed the infected files and requested Google's review, and the site was cleared in about two days.

In 2022 I rebuilt it from a UX designer's desktop, tablet and phone layouts as a React app: Create React App, React 18, react-router, React Bootstrap and Sass, with a customer reviews section and a Get-a-Quote pop-up that emails the company through EmailJS. The quote form produced about nine real customer requests between August and October 2022. The company has since moved to a different site; the link here is my 2022 build.
highlights: Security incident: blacklisted WordPress site cleaned and cleared with Google in about 48 hours
React rebuild from a UX designer's layouts; about nine real quote requests in the first three months
Create React App, React 18, react-router, React Bootstrap, Sass and EmailJS

title: United Homes
summary: Project-portfolio site for a general contractor, built from a UX designer's layouts with per-project pages, photo carousels and a contact form.
description:
United Homes is a general contractor in Sacramento, CA. The site shows finished work project by project and makes it easy to request a quote: per-project routes driven by one projects array, a photo carousel for each, loading states for the image-heavy pages, and a contact form validated with Joi and react-hook-form that delivers through EmailJS.

Built in React with React Bootstrap from the UX designer's Adobe XD layouts, with the design finished in May 2023, the site and form live in June, and twenty revision commits in the following week. I also registered the domain on Route 53 and looked after it for about three years.
highlights: Per-project pages and carousels driven by one data array
Validated contact form delivered through EmailJS
Designer's layouts to a live site in about a week, then domain and DNS for three years

title: R. Cheban Towing
role: Freelance developer, subcontracted by the UX designer
summary: Brochure site for a towing company with click-to-call and a contact form, taken from final design to a working site in four days.
description: R. Cheban Towing is a towing company in South Carolina. The UX designer brought me in to build her design: a four-page site with click-to-call buttons, a contact form validated with Joi and delivered through EmailJS, and smooth-scroll navigation, built in React with React Bootstrap and Sass. Final design arrived on March 25, 2023; the working site was up on March 29. I registered the domain on Route 53.
highlights: Final design to a working site in four days
React, React Bootstrap and Sass; Joi-validated contact form through EmailJS
Built as the UX designer's development partner

title: Accellence Craft & Technique
role: Freelance developer: design and front-end build
summary: Photo-forward Next.js 14 site for a remodeling contractor with every page modeled in Hygraph and fetched server-side through Apollo. Designed and built in late 2023; the client did not launch it.
description:
Accellence Craft & Technique is a remodeling contractor in Anchorage, AK. I designed the site page by page and quoted it, then built it: Next.js 14 App Router with React Server Components, server-side GraphQL through Apollo's Next.js support (experimental at the time), and a full Hygraph content model so the owner could manage hero headers, service cards, the project gallery, the process page and the quote banner without touching code.

The design is photo-forward: full-bleed headers, a portfolio grid, an image slider and a dedicated mobile menu, styled with Tailwind CSS. Built November–December 2023. The owner approved the design, but the site was not launched.
highlights: Next.js 14 with React Server Components and server-side Apollo GraphQL
Whole-site content model in Hygraph for owner-managed content
Own page-by-page design and quote; built, not launched

title: Evolution Gaming & Repair
client: Custom gaming-PC and repair shop, Houston, TX (prospect)
summary: Proposal for a Houston PC shop: replace their template store with a guided PC configurator. The concept build is the early catalog prototype: tiered builds and prebuilt PCs with dynamically routed detail pages.
description:
Evolution Gaming & Repair is a custom gaming-PC builder and repair shop in Houston. I approached them cold in October 2023 with a proposal to replace their template store with a site built around a guided configurator: pick your games, budget and resolution and get recommended components, with cleaner financing and checkout pages.

To show the direction, I built the catalog skeleton in a week: four tiered build packages and a line of prebuilt PCs, each with a dynamically routed detail page generated from a single specs data file, plus financing, events, lounge and FAQ pages. Next.js App Router and Tailwind CSS. The configurator itself was the proposal, not part of the build, and the shop did not take the project. Shown here as a concept.
highlights: Found a business, diagnosed the problem with its store, pitched a recommendation-driven buying experience
Catalog prototype: Next.js dynamic routes generated from one specs data model
Proposal and concept only; the guided configurator was not built

title: Dijkstra Visualizer
summary: Interactive visualizer for Dijkstra's shortest path on a grid, built in React from Clément Mihailescu's pathfinding tutorial with my own interface on top.
description: A React app that shows how Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path on a grid: draw walls by click-dragging, run it, and watch the visited nodes animate and the path trace back. The algorithm and grid follow Clément Mihailescu's pathfinding-visualizer tutorial; the info bar, icons and layout are mine. React class components and state. Deployed to GitHub Pages in August 2022.
highlights: Step-by-step animation of the search and the final path
Click-drag wall drawing on the grid
Built from Clément Mihailescu's tutorial; React class components

title: Tetris
summary: Tetris clone in vanilla JavaScript: game loop, timers, rotation and collision logic, no framework.
description: A Tetris clone in vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS from September 2021, before I used any framework: a setInterval game loop with speed by level, arrow-key rotation and collision, line clearing, score, level and high score, and CSS animations. Direct DOM manipulation here is what later made React's component model click.
highlights: Vanilla JavaScript, no framework
Game loop, timers, rotation and collision logic
Score, levels, high score and CSS animations

title: Asteroids
summary: Asteroids clone in C# and WPF: a XAML interface wired to factory and manager classes, with timers driving the loop.
description: An Asteroids clone in C# on Windows Presentation Foundation. The XAML interface is wired to the game through factory and manager classes for the player and the comets, with Stopwatch timers driving the loop and explosion timing, lives and score, and a saucer enemy above a score threshold. It's where I first paid attention to object lifetimes and cleanup in a hot loop, removing spent projectiles from the canvas explicitly.
highlights: C# and Windows Presentation Foundation (XAML)
Factory and manager classes for player and comets
Timers, frame timing, object lifetimes and cleanup in a hot loop
